presets.title: General
presets.what: The everyday preset: questions, writing, checking things, your own paperwork - one balanced setup instead of a separate admin preset.
presets.cost: qwen3.5:9b sits on the 2060 and holds 196,608 tokens there, taking 9.17 of its 12 GB; nothing else fits beside it. Writing is 44.9 tokens a second, not the fastest.
presets.worse: Not the quickest and not the picture specialist; its thinking has to stay off for ordinary turns, or it answered nothing in the measured run.

presets.title: General Uncensored
presets.focus: general work with the uncensored model
presets.what: General everyday work with the uncensored model, for answers the ordinary model's safety tuning would refuse or water down.
presets.cost: Measured 2026-10-18: cold load 18.5-20.5 s, 45.6 tokens a second at 8k and 45-46 at 16k; 32k loads 7.3 GB at 100% GPU (it only splits across cards when others are resident; no CPU spill). 6.3 GB on disk, Apache-2.0, Qwen3.5 family, 8.95B parameters.
presets.worse: A one-run general rubric of 6 prompts (6/6) is not independent evidence; it did beat the installed qwen2.5-14b fallback on the quality tie and 45.6 against 30.6 tokens a second. Small known nit: it suggested Homebrew on Windows.

measured.source: measurement 2026-10-18: one-run 6-prompt general rubric, 6/6; not independent; 45.6 tok/s at 8k, 45-46 at 16k

presets.title: Coding
presets.what: For writing and fixing code, reading a project, and long tool-driven coding jobs: the 30B coding model on ONE lane that sees both cards, started on demand by this apply.
presets.cost: HEAVY MODE: it fills BOTH GPUs (16.2 GB of video memory here, and another 0.3 GB in system RAM at this window) and pauses the other lanes' models while it works, for about 36 s on a cold load. Measured 2026-11-02 at 16,384 tokens: 85.3 tok/s median on three coding prompts, zero spill. Re-measured 2026-11-03 at 32,768 tokens: 80.4 tok/s median on the same three prompts (79.9 at 16,384, inside this model's own run-to-run noise), with 323.5 MiB of it in system RAM instead of video memory - measured and accepted for this window alone. It is not a single-card model.
presets.worse: Applying it makes it the model chat uses, so the Fast/Live and Agentic+Vision models are NOT resident while it runs - they come back when you apply another preset, and that switch costs a reload. It is not a quick helper: it takes both cards for as long as it is on, and nothing else can be loaded beside it.

measured.source: measurement 2026-10-18 at 28,672 tokens: 76.2 tok/s median eval, 6/6 coding rubric, no CPU spill. The 28,672-token rung was re-measured on 2026-11-02 and no longer loads with zero spill on this PC (212 MiB went to the CPU); 16,384 was the largest rung that loaded with none, and is kept above as that historical fact. From 2026-11-03 the preset asks for 32,768: the whole ladder was measured again through the same shipped path and every rung above 16,384 spills (20,480: 203.5 MiB, 24,576: 207.5, 28,672: 211.5, 32,768: 323.5). At 32,768 it loaded 16,513.7 MiB with 323.5 MiB (0.3 GiB) in system RAM, 79.88 -> 80.36 tok/s median on the three prompts (inside noise), cold load 36.0 s against 37.0 s. That 323.5 MiB is accepted for THIS window only, capped at 352 MiB by jarvis_model_lanes.POOLED_SPILL_ALLOWANCE; every other load still refuses any spill (docs/MEASURED-2026-11-02-POOLED-LANE.md, 2026-11-03 amendment).

presets.heavy_words: This preset needs both cards at once as one pooled lane. While it runs, the everyday and Fast models are paused - they come back, proved from the model list, when you apply another preset. Loading it takes about half a minute.

presets.title: Agentic + Vision
presets.focus: tools, steps, forms, browser, phone, pictures
presets.what: For work that takes several steps with tools - browser, phone, forms, notes - and pictures: the vision model reads the image, and a picture-capable model stays off the display card.
presets.cost: Measured 2026-10-18: it accepts pictures and answered correctly (minor mislabels of status indicators). Browser: 4.45 s to first token, 25.6 s total. Desktop: 0.89 s first token / 46.9 s total warm, 27.6 s / 70.2 s cold - these are LATENCY, not tokens a second.
presets.worse: Slow on the desktop UI (about 47 s warm, 70 s cold for a full answer), and the faster first-token fallback qwen3-vl:8b-thinking produced NO answer on the desktop UI (all thinking, done_reason=length), so it is only a simple-page option.

measured.source: vision test 2026-10-18: pictures accepted, answers correct (minor status-indicator mislabels); speeds are LATENCY, not tok/s

fallback.note: browser 0.39 s first token / 25.9 s total and exact, but on the desktop UI no answer at 3,000 or 700 tokens (all thinking, done_reason=length) - a first-token option for simple pages only, not the default

presets.title: Fast
presets.what: The quickest preset: qwen3.5:4b on the 2080 SUPER at the 16,384-token window its lane serves, while the 2060 keeps the general model warm for when you switch back.
presets.cost: Measured 2026-10-10 on this same card: 77.1 tokens a second and 4.15 GB of video memory at a 65,536-token window (the file is 3.16 GB on disk). The Fast lane starts at 16,384 tokens today, so this row keeps that window; the bigger measurement is why the card has room to spare.
presets.worse: The small model: fastest measured writer here, and the bench's three short prompts were only called broadly correct rather than scored. Chosen for waiting less, not for care; its first request after a cold load is slow on this card.

measured.source: measured 2026-10-10 at 65,536 tokens on the RTX 2080 SUPER (repo restatement: docs/WORK-SETUPS.md:29, jarvis_work.py:262); the Fast lane serves 16,384

presets.title: Reflective Coach
presets.what: For talking something through: a calm listener that reflects what you said first and asks one gentle question at a time. It is the same measured model as General, on the 12 GB card with the same full window, so a conversation is not cut off.
presets.cost: Same measured setup as General: qwen3.5:9b on the 2060 at 196,608 tokens, 44.9 tokens a second, 9.17 of the 12 GB, no spill. No model on this PC has been measured for empathy or reflective quality, and nothing here claims it; pair it with a matching manner in How Jarvis talks once that wording is approved.
presets.worse: A model choice only - it changes no wording by itself. It is not a therapist: it gives no diagnosis, keeps no therapy record and the crisis help stays exactly where it already is.

presets.title: Pictures & Screens
presets.focus: reading a screenshot or a picture
presets.what: For looking at a picture or a screenshot and talking about it: qwen3.5:9b, whose vision capability is documented on this PC, on the 12 GB card. Agentic + Vision is the version that also drives tools.
presets.cost: Same model and card as General at a 32,768-token window. Vision is documented (the model reports completion/vision/tools/thinking and its CLIP encoder runs on the 12 GB card); this row's window and speed are not separately measured. The 2026-10-18 picture test belongs to Agentic + Vision, not this row.
presets.worse: Picture quality through this row is not measured. Live phone-camera frames are explicitly unmeasured, and the old qwen3-vl fallback (which gave no answer on the desktop UI) is not used here.

presets.title: Documents & Notes
presets.what: For long documents, notes and study material: the same measured setup as General - qwen3.5:9b on the 2060 with the full 196,608-token window - named so long reading, note synthesis and study guides are one click instead of remembering which preset has the big window.
presets.cost: Same measured setup as General: 44.9 tokens a second, 9.17 of the 12 GB, no spill. The window is the point - it is what stops a long document being cut before the model sees it.
presets.worse: Not the quickest; fine for reading, not for waiting. Same model as General, so this row adds a named choice and the full window, not a different model.

presets.title: Browser & Forms
presets.focus: long pages and multi-step web work
presets.what: For long web pages and multi-step form work: the long-context model on the 12 GB card with the full 196,608-token window, so a whole page plus its steps fit. Agentic + Vision stays the short tool-loop setup.
presets.cost: Same measured setup as General: qwen3.5:9b on the 2060 at 196,608 tokens, 44.9 tokens a second, 9.17 of the 12 GB, no spill.
presets.worse: Browser and form work has not been measured through this row, and no tool-success rate is claimed; the model is the same one Agentic + Vision already uses.

three_gpu_plan.layout: everyday presets keep one lane per GPU (the everyday lane, the monitor card's lane and the headless card's lane); only on-demand heavy Coding pools the cards on port 11450. Agentic + Vision stays on the everyday card, not the headless one: the 9B weights plus the vision projector need about 7.00 GiB and an 8 GB card with no monitor has 6.65 GiB free, so there is no window at which it fits a headless card

three_gpu_plan.heavy_pooled: on demand, the Coding preset pauses those three lanes and loads qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl on ONE pooled lane on port 11450 across all the cards. It is too big for one card, so this is the ONE case where a model is split across cards; every other preset keeps one lane per GPU.
three_gpu_plan.link_note: the third card likely sits on the B550 chipset through an M.2 adapter: PCIe 3.0 x4, maybe x2. A slower link costs loading time, not a lane; each lane keeps its own model.
three_gpu_plan.future_not_a_preset: Qwen3.8-27B pooled to 28 GB across cards is a future 'max quality' experiment only; it is not a preset and no figure is claimed until it is measured.
